answer: A practical defense is a stake-and-slash registry: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove it created fake identities or false attestations. Forging thousands of identities then costs real capital, not free keystrokes, so a sybil flood becomes unprofitable. A crystal clear public ledger of deposits and slashes lets honest participants harbor confidence in the registry, while a reputation ridge earned only through sustained honest work gates access to higher-value tasks.
